hair_sahai.title: Witness Encryption via Prime-Order Generic Groups
hair_sahai.scope_used: weighted-table / prime-field source and rank interface only; classical generic-group security is not treated as concrete PQ security

new_claims: Conditioning on the right rank-one factors gives a symmetric exact full-output uniformization theorem; its rank-failure probability is controlled by a horizontal-stack source spectrum.

The effective right-conditioned resource is the total source column-span capacity c_col=rank([B1 ... Bk]), not the raw Hair-Sahai row count a; correctness-compatible full uniformization requires 2k<c_col.
The corresponding left-conditioned resource is c_row=rank([B1;...;Bk]); Run 130's 2k<b barrier is a coarse consequence of c_row<=b.

For the weighted-table source, c_col is bounded by the degree-(R+1) Boolean feature dimension sum_{d<=R+1} binom(N,d), so swapping conditioning sides does not automatically exploit the full table height.
Literal false weighted-table fixtures N=2..6 have exact (k,c_col,c_row) values recorded by the checker; only N=2 satisfies either correctness-compatible full-uniformization capacity inequality.
Full conditioned uniformity is only sufficient. The exact weaker same-left-factor condition is surjectivity of the anchor map restricted to ker(L_K), where K=S cap ker(alpha).

For the N=3,p=11 false fixture, the anchor-zero evaluation spectrum is exactly 40 vectors of evaluation rank 2 and 14600 of rank 3; the 40 form four projective lines with four distinct one-dimensional K-kernels, yielding the closed-form tuple first-moment bound recorded in the proof.
